incident.affected: Keplr wallets created with Google or Apple login. Early estimate: about 20% of social-login accounts affected, only a fraction of those actually drained.
incident.attacker: UNKNOWN — no attacker has been publicly named and no verified attacker wallet addresses have been published yet. Whoever controls the stolen funds has not cashed out anything so far.
incident.cause: Security issue at Web3Auth, the social-login provider Keplr uses. Keplr co-founder Josh Lee says the incident originated at Web3Auth, not in Keplr's own code. The full technical root cause has not been published yet.
incident.safe: Wallets created with a recovery (seed) phrase or a hardware wallet (Ledger / Trezor) are NOT affected, per Keplr's initial assessment. MetaMask users are not affected.

timeline.event: Web3Auth pauses its embedded-wallet service after a security issue affecting third parties.
Keplr flags unauthorized transactions on some Google/Apple-login accounts.
Keplr posts its notice: social (Google/Apple) login paused; users told not to add funds or re-import those accounts.
Keplr co-founder Josh Lee: incident originated at Web3Auth; ~20% of social-login accounts affected, only a fraction drained; remaining accounts may be recoverable.
Community trackers report $4.5M+ taken from 41,500+ wallets across Cosmos Hub, Osmosis and Injective; $0 cashed out so far.

incident.title: Keplr / Web3Auth Incident

totals.cashedOutNote: None of the stolen funds has moved / been cashed out yet, per the tracker.
totals.takenNote: Tracker-reported figure (from a community tracker image), at current prices. Keplr/Web3Auth have NOT confirmed a final loss total in their official statements.
